text:
Predicates:
Listed(y) ::: y is listed in Yelp's recommendations.
ReceivedManyNegativeReviews(y) ::: y has received many negative reviews.
Rating(y, r) ::: y has rating r.
Popular(y) ::: y is popular among local residents.
ProvidesTakeOut(y) ::: y provides take-out service.
Store(y) ::: y is a store.
Store(HamdenPlazaSubway) ::: Hamden Plaza Subway store is a store.

Premises:
∀y (Listed(y) → ¬ReceivedManyNegativeReviews(y)) ::: If a restaurant is listed in Yelp's recommendations, then it has not received many negative reviews.
∀y (Rating(y, r) ∧ r > 4 → Listed(y)) ::: All restaurants with rating greater than four are listed in Yelp's recommendations.
∃y (¬ProvidesTakeOut(y) ∧ ReceivedManyNegativeReviews(y)) ::: Some restaurants that do not provide take-out service receive many negative reviews.
∀y (Popular(y) → Rating(y, r) ∧ r > 4) ::: All restaurants that are popular among local residents have ratings greater than four.
Rating(HamdenPlazaSubway, r) ∧ r > 4 ∨ Popular(HamdenPlazaSubway) ::: The Hamden Plaza Subway store has a rating greater than four, or it is popular among local residents.

Conclusion:
(ProvidesTakeOut(HamdenPlazaSubway) ∧ ReceivedManyNegativeReviews(HamdenPlazaSubway)) → (Rating(HamdenPlazaSubway, r) ∧ r > 4 ∧ ¬ProvidesTakeOut(HamdenPlazaSubway))
